hints.text: Tip: Speed is damage. Get going fast enough and your own body becomes the weapon.
Tip: A charged slash releases as a projectile slash and shoves you up and back. Use the recoil.
Tip: Sliding off a slope isn't the same as sliding on flat ground. Gravity has opinions.
Tip: A plunge that lands hard enough knocks back everything nearby. Aim for crowds.
Tip: Switch inventory items without stopping. Standing still is for civilians.
Tip: Wall hangs slowly drain — you're borrowing time, not stopping the clock.
Tip: The grapple hook doesn't care if you let go early. Momentum is yours to keep.
Tip: I-frames during an attack mean a dash through danger is briefer than it looks.
Tip: Gliding slows a fall. It does not forgive a bad dash into a wall.
Tip: Air juggles last longer than the average enemy's patience. Keep swinging.
Tip: Dash doesn't work mid-fall. A slide, on the other hand, has other plans.
Tip: Use the scouting phase before you start the clock. The level isn't going anywhere.
Tip: Restarts are instant on purpose. Die fast. Learn faster. Repeat.
Tip: Hit-stop is a gift. It's one extra frame to admire your own combo.
Tip: Wall jumps work best when you're already committed to the wall. Commit.
Rumor: a slide timed right off the edge of a ramp does more than just slide.
Whisper from the dojo: dash, then dash again. Timing is everything. Allegedly.
Old courier saying: the wall remembers your jump, if you ask it the right way.
Some say a slide in freefall stops being a slide entirely. Ask a ghost.
There's a rhythm to chaining moves no tutorial level will spell out for you.
Veteran couriers don't dash through gaps. They dash through the idea of gaps.
A slope, a jump, and bad intentions — that's not a sentence, that's a technique.
Nobody taught you the wall-cancel. You're supposed to find it. That's the point.
Hint: Killing different kinds of enemies back to back reads better than killing the same one twice.
Hint: A grapple into a bounce into a dash-kill is a sentence the style meter likes to read.
Hint: Stopping to fight is a choice. Flowing through a fight is a better one.
Hint: The style meter doesn't care that it was an accident. It only saw it land.
Did you know? Meiji-era couriers didn't carry katanas that vanish into nothing. You're not exactly normal.
Yastok still can't eat pizza directly. Coat it in ghost grease first. He'll grumble gratefully.
Soul Shards come from astral deliveries. Gold comes from customers who can actually pay you.
Slimes are low-tier spirits who got way too into Halloween. Bounce on them anyway.
Ghosts make excellent grapple points. They rarely file a complaint about it.
Once a samurai, now a pizza ninja. The pay is worse. The pizza is free. Even trade.
NYPD stands for Ninja Yakuza Pizza Delivery. No relation to any actual police department. Mikey checked. Mostly.
Yastok doesn't take gold. He takes knowledge, perks, and the occasional cryptic sign.
Mikey says: 'I'm not superstitious. But I am a little stitious about cold pizza.'
Mikey's Employee Handbook, page 1: 'Speed is damage. Also don't be late. Also deliver the pizza.'
Mikey once tried delivering a pizza by dashing through a wall. HR is still reviewing the footage.
Mikey's motto: 'I don't want to be the boss of a ninja delivery gang. I want to be the FRIEND who's also the boss.'
Mikey insists NYPD stands for 'Nice Young Pizza Delivery.' He is wrong about this. And several other things.
Mikey tried to cut a pizza mid-air once. We're still finding pepperoni in the rafters.
Mikey's pep talk before your shift: 'You miss every shortcut you don't dash for. Wait — that's basketball. Same thing.'
Mikey's review of the new ghost hires: 'Great attendance. Zero punctuality. Can't hold a pizza box. Three stars.'
Mikey, watching you take damage: 'That's what the HP bar said.'
Mikey's business plan: 'Step one, deliver the pizza fast. Step two, there is no step two. We just go faster.'
Mikey challenged the training dummy to a duel. The dummy won. He's renamed it 'Senpai.'
Mikey's idea of stealth: standing in plain sight, yelling 'I AM NOT HERE.'
Mikey on the rival gang's boss: 'He's basically me, if I had money and self-control.'
Mikey's self-inflicted pizza-to-the-face count this week: twelve. He is very proud of this.
Mikey's final word on the job: 'We're not just delivering pizza. We're delivering it FAST, with STYLE, occasionally into a ghost's face. That's the dream.'
